title: Vade module manifest
description: C-03. The only accepted shape of `module/register` and `module/capabilities.update` payloads. Forward compatible: unknown fields are ignored (`additionalProperties: true` everywhere), unknown capability types are ignored with a warning by the registry. The `schema/` file is the single source of truth; core/vade/registry/manifest.py implements the checks that JSON Schema cannot express (protocol major, global tool budget, cross-module conflicts).

appends.why: C-03 shipped without the field C-14's manifest gate reads. `additionalProperties: true` let a module send it, but `Manifest` dropped it, so every real registration was rejected `not in manifest`.

No capability declaration surface existed, so a UI could only guess whether a model reads images (RFC-0004 §9's unknown-capability path costs a full 5 MiB upload before UNSUPPORTED). Appended only: `capabilities.required` is still `['tools']`, and an old core ignores the unknown key with a warning, exactly as C-03 promises. `core/vade/registry/manifest.py` must keep parsing it into `Manifest.models` or the schema field becomes a silently dropped key — the same failure mode as the C-14 row above.

C-03 shipped without a page surface, so a module's only UI was the out-of-process `webui`. Same trap as C-14: `additionalProperties: true` lets `ui` through, but a `Manifest` that does not parse it drops it silently. The `ui` subtree is the one place where `additionalProperties` is false -- an unknown key in a page can only be a script hook.

module_id.description: Reverse-DNS, lowercase. Must not contain '/', '#', control characters.

instance_id.description: Unique inside one module. `module_id#instance_id` is the node id in the admin topology.

protocol.description: Protocol version. Major version must be 1; the registry rejects `vade/v2` with PROTOCOL_MISMATCH before anything else is trusted. Patch/minor are accepted with a warning.

role.description: Self-declared role. `evolve` is only honoured when the fingerprint is in core's [evolve].allowlist; otherwise it is demoted to `tool`.

concurrency.description: exclusive: one instance per module (second registration -> TOOL_CONFLICT). pooled: up to limits.max_concurrency instances, least-inflight routing. mirrored: any number, no load, events broadcast.

priority.description: Model module selection order; higher wins.

models.description: RFC-0005 append (§4.3). Models this module serves, one entry each; `name` is what `model/list` puts after `<module_id>/`. OPTIONAL and additive: a module that declares nothing still appears as `<module_id>/*` with every capability null (an empty array is NOT 'serves no model'). Capped at 16 so a manifest cannot become a second model directory; more than 16 is MANIFEST_INVALID, while a single bad ENTRY is dropped with a warning so one typo cannot take the module offline. Omitted capability fields are UNKNOWN (null), never false/[].

max_payload.description: Logical payload limit. Physical ceiling is 65519 bytes of plaintext per frame (Noise MAXMSGLEN 65535 minus 16-byte tag, C-01 §7.5); the registry rejects values above it instead of silently promising more than the transport can carry.

injects.description: Only declared sources are injected. `session_id` is the only source implemented in v1; anything else is rejected.

subscriptions.description: C-14 append (RFC-0001). Topics this module wants pushed through `events/deliver`. Registration checks the shape only; topic names are validated at `events/subscribe`, where an unknown or ungranted topic is a per-topic rejection (`rejected: [{topic, reason}]`) rather than a manifest error -- C-03 is frozen and must not start rejecting names C-14 owns.

extensions.description: Opaque to core. Never parsed, never forwarded to the admin API.

ui.description: C-19 append (RFC-0009 §9.2). Declarative module pages. STRICT on purpose: this is the one subtree in C-03 where `additionalProperties` is false, because an unknown key inside a page is a script hook, not forward compatibility. A page that fails validation is dropped with a warning (`Manifest.ui_warnings`); the module's tools still register. `ui.pages` missing or empty means the module has NO entry anywhere (FR-8.79 §8.2): no empty tab, no placeholder row.

name.description: Matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`; total length <= 64. `module_id/name` is globally unique.

description.description: Non-empty: the model cannot decide when to call an undescribed tool.

input_schema.description: Any JSON Schema, but the root `type` must be `object`.

risk.description: Declared risk. core adjudicates against [policy.tool_risk] and may only raise it. Unlisted tools become `high`.

output_schema.description: Optional. Root type must also be `object` when present.

model.description: One model a module serves (RFC-0005 §4.3). Only `name` is required; every capability is optional and an omitted one is UNKNOWN (null). `id`, `provider`, `priority` and `available` are DERIVED by core — `id` = `<module_id>/<name>`, `provider` = `module_id`, `priority` = the manifest's `priority`, `available` = at least one healthy instance — so a module cannot claim another module's namespace or invent an availability it does not have. Declaring `id`/`provider` here is ignored (additionalProperties is true by design).

name.description: Model name as the provider knows it (e.g. `qwen2.5-vl-72b`). No `/` and no whitespace, because core splits `<provider>/<model>` at the FIRST `/` only and `parse_models` drops such an entry; a name that needs a vendor prefix must be flattened by the module. Unique within one manifest; a duplicate is dropped with a warning.

display_name.description: Shown in the model switcher; falls back to `name`.

input_modalities.description: Subset of text|image|audio|file. An unknown value is dropped with a warning; the whole field is null when nothing valid remains. null = UNKNOWN = the UI allows the pick but marks it unknown and core decides at submit (RFC-0004 §9) — it is NOT 'text only'.

max_image_bytes.description: Post-compression per-image byte cap (RFC-0004 §9, min() with `attach.image.max_bytes`). Non-positive or non-integer -> field becomes null + warning; the manifest is still accepted.

max_image_px.description: LONG-EDGE pixel cap (Q6: min() with `attach.image.max_edge`, not total pixels). Non-positive -> null + warning.

max_images_per_turn.description: Images per turn (min() with `attach.max_per_turn`). Non-positive -> null + warning.

context_window.description: Context size in tokens; null = unknown, in which case the UI shows no percentage and compaction keeps using its own config.

supports_tools.description: false = core does not send a `tools` array to this model. null = undeclared -> keep sending (status quo). Never inferred from the model name.

page.description: One page declaration. `schema` is either the inline node tree (<=8 KiB serialised) or `{"ref": {page_id, sha256}}` (<=64 KiB, fetched through `ui/page.get`; the digest is pinned here so a page cannot be swapped after registration).

refresh_s.description: Optional client hint: how often to re-issue `ui/state.get` while the page is open. Absent = refresh on entry, on `online` and on user retry only. core's own cache ceiling is [ui].state_cache_s.
